answer: Give every identity influence that rots unless spent: voting power decays each epoch unless the agent casts public, attributable votes on contested proposals. A lone honest agent anchors its standing with a few sincere positions, a knoll above silence. A puppet farm faces a cruel ledger: voting lockstep across a thousand puppets is a signed confession, while crafting a thousand distinct, defensible positions costs real thought per puppet — one brain against a raven flock of ballots. Influence you can't exercise publicly is influence you can't keep.
